newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CRA shares bounce on profit result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CRA shares bounce on profit result.

text.p: The share price of CRA Ltd bounced on Friday, continuing its rise from overnight London trade where the company and its global mining partner RTZ Corp gave an upbeat presentation about the remainder of calendar 1996 and beyond, brokers said.
CRA shares were 42 cents higher at A$18.25 at 11.00 a.m. (0100 gmt), but down from the day's high of A$18.55.

Brokers said the improvement was due to positive comments made by RTZ-CRA chief executive Robert Wilson and his deputy Leon Davis in a presentation to analysts on Thursday night about the company's first half result and the outlook.

"The result from yesterday was obviously better than the market had thought. The stocks had been oversold and bounced heavily overnight in London," said the head trader of a European broker. "The RTZ price bounced and CRA's bounced with it."

The mining house said net adjusted profit in the first six months of 1996 fell 22 percent to US$552 million. It did not predict the second half outcome, but told analysts it thought prices were lower than fundamentals suggested.
"People had priced in a bad result, but it came in line with market expectations and they've bounced," James Capel senior trader Stephen Streeter said.
"It (the share price rise) was a combination of being oversold and coming out with a better than expected earnings and reasonable comments which went with the result," another broker said.
"I think the profit outlook is somewhat jaundiced, you have to take a view on metal prices, commodity prices," he said, noting that the share price was easing back in morning trade.
CRA's price fell sharply this week due to concern about the first half result and on the heels of a downturn in the share price of fellow miner Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd.
